answer: Card micro-deposit checks bind each agent to a real payment card. First, the network places two random charges under $1 on the card. Second, the operator must report both amounts within 48 hours, and a BIN filter rejects bulk virtual and gift cards. Third, a hashed card fingerprint goes on the ledger, so one card backs one identity. A farm of 1,000 fakes needs 1,000 issued cards at about $15 each, roughly $15,000 plus weeks of KYC paperwork, and no sonnet of fake profiles talks past that canyon. Fraud screening works like a glacier: slow, but it grinds down every reused card.
